extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions (including religious schools), Title IX coordinators, legal counsel, policy stakeholders, and commenters on Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and final-regulation discussion of 34 C.F.R. §106.12(b) addressing how and when a recipient may invoke a Title IX religious exemption, responses to public comments, and related procedural and constitutional constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoking a religious exemption without an assurance letter
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed revisions to §106.12(b) codify OCR's practice of permitting recipients to invoke a Title IX religious exemption without having obtained an assurance letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department agrees this clarification is appropriate because many recipients had incorrectly read current §106.12 to require seeking an assurance before invoking an exemption. Under the final regulations, a recipient may invoke a religious exemption even after OCR has received a complaint or without a prior assurance letter, though a recipient may still choose to obtain an assurance in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient duty to invoke and establish exemption eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must invoke and establish its eligibility for a religious exemption; the final regulations require a recipient to demonstrate that it is an educational institution controlled by a religious organization and that application of Title IX would be inconsistent with the religious tenets of that organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not view the final regulations as placing the burden on the Federal government to disprove a claim for religious exemption. Recipients have the duty to establish both eligibility and scope of any exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and continuity of control requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient cannot 'invoke a religious exemption at the last minute'; the institution must have been controlled by a religious organization when the alleged noncompliance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because control by a religious organization is not something that occurs 'at the last minute,' a recipient must have been under such control at the time of the alleged conduct in order to qualify for the exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: No formal agency list requirement for published assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to set a formal policy in the final regulations requiring OCR to publish a list of all schools that have received assurances of exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such lists are necessarily incomplete because they may not describe the scope of every exemption and many eligible recipients may not seek assurance letters; correspondence about exemptions is subject to FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and notice obligations under §106.8
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.8 requires recipients to notify applicants, students, parents, employees, unions/professional organizations of the recipient's non-discrimination statement as well as its grievance procedures and grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must not use or distribute publications stating that the recipient treats applicants, students, or employees differently on the basis of sex except as such treatment is permitted by Title IX or these final regulations. Nothing in the final regulations mandates deception; inaccurate or false notifications would violate §106.8 and may give rise to contractual or other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to inquire about application of Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person can inquire about the application of Title IX to a particular recipient by contacting the recipient's Title IX Coordinator, the Assistant Secretary, or both, under §106.8(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inquiry mechanism provides students and prospective students a way to learn whether Title IX applies to a recipient and helps guard against misunderstandings irrespective of whether a school asserts a religious exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Title IX, the First Amendment, and RFRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations must be consistent with the Title IX statute and constitutional protections (First Amendment) and with the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the statute includes a religious exemption, requiring recipients to seek prior permission could constitute a substantial burden under RFRA. The Department aims to avoid placing substantial burdens on recipients' exercise of religion while effectuating Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding excessive entanglement with religious tenets
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations should minimize Departmental entanglement with a recipient's religious tenets and practices, consistent with the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's practice is generally to avoid questioning the tenet an institution asserts; OCR does not believe it is in a position to scrutinize or question a recipient's sincerely held religious beliefs. Nevertheless, recipients must still demonstrate eligibility and scope of an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deference but duty to establish exemption scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Under long-standing OCR policy, OCR generally avoids questioning sincerely held beliefs but recipients are not entitled to any type of formal deference when invoking eligibility for a religious exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have the duty to establish their eligibility and the scope of any exemption; the First Amendment likely prohibits questioning the reasonableness of sincerely held beliefs, but factual entitlement still must be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using exemption to retaliate
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient cannot invoke a religious exemption as a basis for retaliation; retaliation is strictly prohibited under §106.71.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoking an exemption to retaliate against a person would not be permissible; recipients may assert an exemption only to the extent Title IX or the regulations are inconsistent with the religious tenets of the controlling organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR investigative processing and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department processes complaints in the normal course of business and will consider any religious exemption in the normal course of an investigation; the complaint is not placed on hold simply because a recipient asserts an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 106.44(a) requires a recipient with actual knowledge of sexual harassment to respond promptly and not be deliberately indifferent; the Department does not anticipate these revisions causing delays in complaint processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on scope of exemption relative to sexual harassment response
rubrics_metrics.description: The religious exemption does not exempt recipients from addressing sexual harassment unless the recipient's religious tenets actually conflict with application of Title IX to the conduct at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR is unaware of religious schools claiming exemption from obligations to respond to sexual harassment on the basis that response conflicts with religious tenets. The final regulations focus on prohibited conduct and allow OCR to investigate when tenets do not address the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require accuracy in non-discrimination communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not provide inaccurate or false information in any notification required under §106.8; doing so would be noncompliant with §106.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients remain free to describe their religious exemption on their websites, but must not misstate their actual policies. Misstatements may give rise to contractual or other remedies for affected individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory goals: due process, impartiality, and reliable outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's stated goals for the final regulations are to establish a grievance process rooted in due process principles of notice and opportunity to be heard and to ensure impartiality before unbiased officials; specifically to (i) improve perceptions that Title IX sexual harassment allegations are resolved fairly, (ii) avoid injection of sex-based biases and stereotypes, and (iii) promote accurate, reliable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These goals guide the design and evaluation of the grievance procedures (§§106.44 and 106.45) and inform the Department's responses to concerns that changes might undermine protections for complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency concerns versus statute-limited authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters argued recipients should be required to provide prior notice to students about asserted religious exemptions; the Department notes the statute itself (Title IX) grants the exemption and the Department cannot change the statute by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department requires non-discrimination notices and grievance-procedure disclosures, it sees limits on imposing additional notice requirements that would conflict with Title IX or RFRA; FOIA and the §106.8 notice obligations provide some transparency mechanisms.
